Heat Sink: Thermal Compliance with Temperature BCs

Description

This tutorial demonstrates heat conduction topology optimization with multiple temperature boundary conditions. A distributed heat flux enters the top edge, while the left edge is held at T = 100 and the right edge at T = 0 (acting as heat-sink fins). The optimizer redistributes a fixed volume of high-conductivity material to dissipate heat most efficiently.

Unlike the simpler HeatTree benchmark, this problem has asymmetric temperature BCs on both sides, creating complex heat flow patterns that challenge the optimizer to find efficient conduction paths.

Setup

using TopOpt, LinearAlgebra

Define the Problem

nels = (60, 30)         # mesh resolution (60×30 elements)
sizes = (1.0, 1.0)      # element sizes
k = 1.0                 # thermal conductivity
heatflux = Dict("top" => 100.0)  # heat flux on top boundary (W/m²)
V = 0.5                 # volume fraction constraint

# Tleft=100 and Tright=0 fix temperatures at left and right edges
# (heat-sink fins), while flux enters from the top
problem = HeatConductionProblem(
    Val{:Linear}, nels, sizes, k;
    Tleft=100.0, Tright=0.0, heatflux=heatflux
)

println("Created heat conduction problem with $(TopOpt.getncells(problem)) elements")

The boundary conditions: - Top edge: Distributed heat flux (100 W/m²) - Left edge: Fixed temperature T = 100 (hot fin) - Right edge: Fixed temperature T = 0 (cold fin) - Bottom edge: Insulated

FEA Solver and Objective

solver = FEASolver(DirectSolver, problem; xmin=0.001)
comp = ThermalCompliance(solver)
vol = TopOpt.Volume(solver; fraction=true)
filter = DensityFilter(solver; rmin=2.0)

f = x -> comp(filter(PseudoDensities(x)))
g = x -> [vol(filter(PseudoDensities(x))) - V]

Thermal compliance J = QᵀT measures work done by boundary heat flux against the temperature field. Minimizing it drives heat toward both temperature boundaries efficiently.

Run Optimization

x0 = fill(V, length(solver.vars))

println("Starting topology optimization...")
println("Volume constraint: $V")
println("Number of design variables: $(length(x0))")
println("Initial objective value (thermal compliance): $(f(x0))")

model = Model(f)
addvar!(model, zeros(length(x0)), ones(length(x0)))
add_ineq_constraint!(model, g)
alg = MMA87()
options = MMAOptions(; tol=Tolerance(; kkt=1e-4))
result = optimize(model, alg, x0; options=options)

println("\nOptimization complete!")
println("Final objective value (thermal compliance): $(result.minimum)")
println("Iterations: $(result.iter)")
